content.title: About
content.content: Corn taco shells are thin, crunchy tortillas made from whole‑grain corn flour, water and salt. They are a staple of Mexican cuisine, used for tacos, tostadas and many other dishes. The shell has a characteristic golden hue and a pleasant corn aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn tortillas originated in Mexico over 3,000 years ago and form the basis of the traditional diet.
Traditionally they are cooked on a stone griddle (comal), but most are now mass‑produced in industrial ovens.
The corn used provides natural carotenoids, giving the shells their yellowish color.
Corn shells are gluten‑free, making them suitable for people with celiac disease.
In the United States more than 3 billion corn tortillas are consumed each year.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Corn shells contain dietary fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with wheat tortillas, corn shells have a lower fat content, making them a lighter option.

items.title: Source of vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium helps maintain normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Corn shells can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties contain added salt; choose low‑sodium options if you monitor sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use shells as a base for tacos, burritos, quesadillas, or as a crunchy side. Warm them on a skillet, microwave, or oven. For a softer texture, soak in hot water for a few minutes before filling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep shells in an airtight package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent drying out. Discard any shells that develop mold or an off‑odor.
